headline: Police pursue charges after two fights disrupt Whitman-Hanson football game
dek: Hanson police say one juvenile was held after an alleged assault on officers and that a second fight involved an alleged head-stomping and a possible knife.
body: Police are pursuing possible criminal charges after two fights broke out during a Whitman-Hanson Regional High School football game Friday night, including one incident in which a juvenile allegedly assaulted officers and another in which a student allegedly stomped on another juvenile's head. The game was being played between Whitman-Hanson and Silver Lake Regional High School. The accounts from [WCVB](https://www.wcvb.com/article/hanson-high-school-football-students-fight-charges/74005213), [WHDH 7News](https://whdh.com/news/teens-may-face-criminal-charges-after-fights-at-whitman-hanson-football-game/) and the [Boston Globe](https://www.bostonglobe.com/2026/10/03/metro/whitman-hanson-football-game-fights/) describe allegations, not adjudicated findings.

Hanson police said officers were already assigned to the game when the first fight broke out among students. Officers and school staff tried to de-escalate the conflict and removed several students from the event because of what police called inappropriate behavior. One juvenile refused to comply with officers' orders and allegedly assaulted them while they were breaking up the fight. Police took that juvenile to the Hanson Police Department to await a parent or guardian, according to the Boston Globe, and said the case could be sent to juvenile court by summons.

A second fight happened later in the game. Police said a juvenile repeatedly kicked and stomped on another juvenile's head. Officials also received a report that a knife may have been displayed during the confrontation, although the weapon was not reported as being used in the fight. Several people involved in that altercation left before officers arrived. As of Saturday afternoon, police had not announced additional arrests, and investigators were still working to identify everyone involved and determine each person's role.

The incident drew a response from more than the two officers assigned to the game. Whitman police and the Hanson Fire Department also assisted, according to the Globe. The game itself was not described in the reports as a confrontation between the teams; the people involved were spectators and students, rather than players engaged in a football play. That distinction matters for families and school officials trying to separate the conduct under investigation from the athletic event and the large majority of students who attended without being involved.

Whitman-Hanson Regional High School Principal Christopher Jones said in a statement carried by 7News that the school did not condone the behavior and that it did not represent most of the students who came to support the teams. The statement acknowledged the seriousness of the incidents without identifying the juveniles or describing disciplinary decisions. Because the people under investigation are minors, the police and news reports did not publish their names.

The possible knife report remains one of the unanswered questions. WCVB and the Globe both said police received a report that a knife was brandished, but the reports also said it was not used in the fight. Police have not announced that a knife was recovered, and no account reviewed for this article described a confirmed weapon-related charge. That leaves the allegation subject to the continuing investigation rather than treating it as an established fact.

The case also illustrates the limits of security assigned to school sporting events. Two police details were present before the first fight, but officers still had to manage separate disturbances involving juveniles, spectators leaving the area and a possible weapon. The reports do not say whether the game ended early, whether the teams faced athletic penalties or what additional security steps the district may consider. Those decisions would come from school administrators and athletic officials, not from the criminal investigation alone.

Hanson police said criminal charges may be sought after the investigation is complete. For the first juvenile, that process may involve a summons to juvenile court; for the second fight, police said charges remain dependent on identifying the participants and determining what each person did. No final charging decision has been announced for every person involved. The investigation remains active, and the juveniles are presumed innocent unless prosecutors prove the allegations in court. Sources: [WCVB](https://www.wcvb.com/article/hanson-high-school-football-students-fight-charges/74005213), [WHDH 7News](https://whdh.com/news/teens-may-face-criminal-charges-after-fights-at-whitman-hanson-football-game/) and the [Boston Globe](https://www.bostonglobe.com/2026/10/03/metro/whitman-hanson-football-game-fights/).
